User: Make it quick, I'm on a job site. Forty-five seconds.
Agent: Totally—I'll be quick. Did you call because you saw our ad/voicemail, or were you just searching for a way to stop missing calls?

Agent: Yes—when you can’t pick up, Dialux answers, captures the details, and gets the caller booked or routed so you don’t lose the job. When a call hits you today, what usually happens—voicemail or a receptionist?
User: Voicemail mostly. I need something that grabs those calls and books them. How much and how soon?
Agent: Got it—voicemail mostly, and you want it to grab those callers and book them. For pricing and timeline, it depends on your booking setup (what calendar/CRM are you using today?)
User: Google Calendar. Just tell me the cost and when you can start. Crews are waiting.
Agent: Got it—Google Calendar. Typical ranges are **$3–9K setup** and **$1.2–2.8K/month**, and once Jay plugs it into your Google Calendar we can usually start **in days, not weeks**—what kind of jobs are you booking (remodels, GC work, something else)?
User: Landscaping. Skip the details. If it catches those calls, it pays for itself. What's next?
Agent: Makes sense—and yeah, landscaping calls don’t wait. Ballpark, how many calls a week hit voicemail right now: 10, 20, 30?
User: About 25 calls missed weekly. Forty-five percent would book, average job around $900. That's revenue slipping through. Next step?
Agent: Got it—at your numbers you’re leaking about **$43,800/month** from missed calls. It’s a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay so you can see exactly how it would capture and book those calls—what’s better for you, **later today or tomorrow**?
User: Fine, if it catches those calls it pays for itself. Tomorrow, earliest time. Number +13055550003. Done?
Agent: Got it—tomorrow morning works. Before I line it up, what’s your first name?
User: Boris. Now, send the confirmation. Crews are waiting, and I need to get back to work.
Agent: Got it, Boris—before I can send the confirmation, what’s your last name?
User: Petrov. Just send the confirmation quickly. I need to get back to work.
Agent: Got it, Boris Petrov—what’s the name of your landscaping company?
User: Petrov Landscaping. Now, about the demo—send the details. I’ve got machinery running and can’t waste more time.
Agent: Got it—Petrov Landscaping. And quick check: are you on **Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific** time?
User: Eastern. Miami, FL. Now let's wrap this up. Send the confirmation, I’ve got machinery waiting.
Agent: One moment while I check availability... I can get you in tomorrow at **2:45 PM** or **6:30 PM** Eastern—which works?
User: 2:45 PM works. Send the details to my number. I've got to get back to the site.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Boris—you're booked for **tomorrow at 2:45 PM Eastern**. You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details—you can add it to your calendar in one click, or reschedule if you need to; is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Make it fast. I have machinery to handle and crews waiting. Time is money.
Agent: Totally hear you. You’ll get an SMS with the confirmation details for tomorrow at 2:45 PM Eastern—add it to your calendar or reschedule if you need to. Really glad you called; Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great rest of your day—bye.
